content: Lentinan, derived from Lentinus edodes (shiitake mushroom), is administered at a dosage of 1-4 mg intravenously (IV) or intramuscularly (IM) once per week. It is used as an adjunctive treatment for cancer and HIV. Evidence suggests it may be possibly effective when combined with didanosine in HIV management. However, there is insufficient evidence to definitively rate its efficacy as an adjunctive treatment for breast, gastric, or prostate cancer. Preliminary studies indicate potential improvement in these conditions, but no conclusive results have been established. Adverse effects associated with lentinan include thrombocytopenia. Chronic consumption of large doses of whole shiitake mushrooms has been linked to dermatitis and eosinophilia. Hypersensitivity reactions have also been reported. Regarding pregnancy, lentinan falls under Pregnancy Category A, which means it is generally considered acceptable. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. However, specific data on lactation and its safety during breastfeeding are not available.
